content: {"summary":"On 3 Aug 2025 a credential‑stuffing attack generated roughly ten‑times the normal login attempts. Auth‑service pods, capped at 64 concurrent logins and running at their CPU limit, returned 503, which the edge propagated. Raising the pods’ CPU limit stopped the 503s, but the edge had no rate‑limit on the login route, so the overload was not mitigated at the edge.","likely_cause":"Credential‑stuffing overload combined with auth‑service pods hitting their CPU limit and internal 503 caps, amplified by lack of edge rate‑limiting on the login route.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Login attempts spiked from ~15 rps to ~150 rps, indicating credential stuffing","evidence_ids":["INC-0067#0"],"quote":"attempts had gone from the usual 15 or so a second to about 150 a second"},{"text":"Auth‑service pods cap at 64 in‑flight logins and answer 503 when exceeded","evidence_ids":["INC-0067#0"],"quote":"once 64 logins are in flight it answers `503`"},{"text":"Both auth‑service pods were running at their CPU limit (2 cores)","evidence_ids":["INC-0067#1"],"quote":"both pods were sitting exactly at their CPU limit."},{"text":"Raising the CPU limit to 4 cores per pod stopped the 503 responses despite continued traffic","evidence_ids":["INC-0067#1"],"quote":"The `503`s stopped at 10:34"},{"text":"The edge has no rate limit on the /v1/auth/login route","evidence_ids":["INC-0067#1"],"quote":"There is no rate limit on the login route at the edge"}],"next_checks":["Check current CPU limits and autoscaling configuration for auth‑service pods","Implement rate limiting on /v1/auth/login at the edge gateway","Add alert for high share of failed login attempts","Review auth‑service capacity and concurrency settings for burst traffic"]}
